findings.title: Fallback locales are only preloaded inside ApplicationController, so fallbacks fail outside web requests
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so the fallback chain returned by `FallbackLocaleList` (current locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, `:en`) is only loaded into the `Simple` backend during HTTP requests. Any translation performed outside a controller — mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, `rails runner`, console — goes through `I18n.translate`, which only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. Because the default/`:en` files were never loaded, the `Fallbacks` backend's `super(fallback, ...)` lookups find nothing and the fallback silently does not happen. For a server-side fallback feature this means the behavior only works for requests; e.g. notification emails generated in jobs will still show missing translations instead of falling back to the site default/English. The fallback locales should be ensured-loaded from `translate`/`load_locale` (or lazily from the backend) rather than only from the controller filter.

findings.title: Fallback resolver depends on SiteSetting (DB) and can raise during boot/CLI
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`. This method is invoked by the i18n `Fallbacks` backend on every translation miss, so the global fallback resolver now depends on `SiteSetting`/the database. During boot or CLI tasks where the `site_settings` table or `SiteSetting` is not ready (e.g. fresh `rake db:migrate`, `assets:precompile`, early initializers, `rails runner` before DB connection), a translation miss will call into `SiteSetting.default_locale` and can raise instead of simply returning a missing translation. In addition, `.compact` is applied after `.to_sym`, so it cannot protect against a nil `default_locale`; if `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil this raises `NoMethodError` before `compact` can filter it. Guard/normalize the value and avoid depending on the DB from this hot global resolver.

findings.title: Fallbacks are now enabled globally (including test/development) with no tests
findings.body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` existed only in `config/environments/production.rb`, `config/environments/profile.rb`, and `config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb`; this initializer turns fallbacks on for every environment. In development/test, where fallbacks were previously off, missing translations will now silently resolve to the site default/English instead of surfacing, which can mask i18n regressions and break any tests that assert on missing-translation behavior. The PR also adds no tests exercising the new fallback chain (user locale -> site default -> English) or the new `ensure_loaded!` path, so this behavior change is unverified.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! mutates shared @loaded_locales outside the LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and then reads `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it (`@loaded_locales = []`). On the first concurrent requests multiple threads can each evaluate `@loaded_locales ||= []` against a nil/being-reset value, creating/assigning competing arrays, so previously-recorded loaded locales can be dropped and files reloaded redundantly; a reader can also observe a half-updated array. The nil-init and membership check should be done inside the existing mutex (or `load_locale` should be relied on for the synchronized check).
